papers_read.title_as_printed: Identification of Mild cognitive impairment based on quadruple GCN model constructed with multiple features from higher-order brain connectivity (Li et al., Expert Syst Appl 2023)
Optimal transport- and kernel-based early detection of mild cognitive impairment patients based on magnetic resonance and positron emission tomography images (Liu et al., Alzheimer's Res Ther 2022)

what_each_reports.P-75: MCI (117) vs normal control (113) from ADNI using tau PET (18F-AV-1451) and amyloid PET (18F-AV-45) regional protein features, higher-order sparse-regression networks, self-attention GCN pooling and a quadruple Siamese network: ACC 0.935 +/- 0.022, SEN 0.903, SPE 0.895, AUC 0.922 (MPHN(H++)-SAGCN). The validation scheme is not specified beyond reported mean +/- SD.
what_each_reports.P-194: Early MCI (273) vs late MCI (187) from ADNI using FDG-PET and VBM-MRI ROI features (116 each), optimal-transport transfer learning from AD vs NC, bootstrap aggregation. Ten-fold CV best ACC 68.76 +/- 7.53% (FDG, AUC 0.66); held-out 20% test after bagging: best ACC 75.00% (FDG, SD L1l2/linear, AUC 0.77), best AUC 0.79; baselines 52.4-64.7%.

quantity_a: Accuracy for MCI vs cognitively normal classification from tau and amyloid PET in ADNI (n = 230).
quantity_b: Accuracy for early-MCI vs late-MCI stratification from FDG-PET and structural MRI VBM features in ADNI (n = 460 target subjects).
incompatible_if_same: No. The comparisons differ (MCI vs NC against EMCI vs LMCI, the latter a much subtler within-MCI split that P-194 itself says has a small effect size), so a lower accuracy for EMCI vs LMCI does not refute a higher accuracy for MCI vs NC. Neither paper claims a result about the other's task.

gates.task: mismatch at the comparison level: P-75 MCI vs NC; P-194 EMCI vs LMCI (both coded T1 in the registry, but the classes differ)
gates.dataset_family: match: ADNI (possible participant overlap, not quantified)
gates.validation_tier: nominally V2 in both; P-75 does not state its split/CV scheme, P-194 uses 10-fold CV plus an 80/20 hold-out
gates.modality_family: mismatch: tau and amyloid PET (molecular PET) in P-75 vs FDG-PET plus structural MRI VBM in P-194; the record's 'Neuroimaging' bucket hides this

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both report accuracy, but on different class pairs (MCI vs NC vs EMCI vs LMCI) and different input modalities
performance_validity: flag does not apply: P-75 reports 93.5% accuracy (below 0.97) and P-194 at most 75%; the comparison is a performance comparison on different tasks
independence: Distinct studies, different authors; both draw on ADNI.
grounds: P-75's 93.5% is accuracy for MCI vs normal controls from tau and amyloid PET networks.
P-194 classifies early vs late MCI, not MCI vs controls, from FDG-PET and VBM features, and its reported accuracies are 56.8-75.0%; no 53% figure is its headline result.
Different class pair and different modality families mean the 93.5 vs 53 gap is not a disagreement on one quantity.

evidence_quotes.quote: Our proposed MCI identification method was evaluated on 230 subjects (including 117 MCI subjects, 113 normal control subjects) with both 18F-AV-1451 PET and 18F-AV-45 PET data
We have developed an optimal transport based transfer learning model to discriminate between early and late MCI.
Based on FDG features, our model achieved 68.76 ± 7.53% accuracy and 0.66 ± 0.08 AUC score across ten-fold cross-validation.

record_defects: claim_b 'P-194: Acc 53 on T1' does not match the paper: P-194's own method reports 56.79-75.00% accuracy; the nearest figure, 52.44%, is the SUBA benchmark on VBM, a comparator, not P-194's result.
The record treats both as the same T1 comparison, but P-194 is EMCI vs LMCI, not MCI vs NC.
modality_family 'Neuroimaging' conflates molecular PET (tau/amyloid) with FDG-PET plus structural MRI; the registry lists P-75 modality_subtype as PET and P-194 as MRI/PET.
The G4 note describes P-194 as an 'auxiliary-task transfer model' on the same task; it is transfer learning from AD vs NC to a different target task (EMCI vs LMCI).
resolution_status 'partially_resolved_candidate' cites a list of other papers' scores, which explains no specific condition separating these two results.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A second study of MCI vs NC from tau/amyloid PET in ADNI with an accuracy whose uncertainty excludes 93.5%, or of EMCI vs LMCI with FDG/VBM features excluding P-194's range.
